To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantum well reflectance is strongly modulated due to the quantum well discrete excitation levels, the modulation period depends on the pulse duration, and the modulation depth depends on the ratio of the radiative to non-radiative relaxation times.
the quantum wells can be stimulated by light pulse of any arbitrary form and the light reflectance and the absorbance are calculated.
The light reflection and absorption of the quantum well are determined by the pulse and monochromic light stimulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties of a semiconductor QW in the case of an arbitrary form of the stimulating pulse and the arbitrary relationship between the radiative and the non-radiative relaxation.
the influence of the quantum well parameters on the optical characteristics of QW in the presence of a stimulating pulse.
the light absorption in the QW in the presence of two closely situated exciton levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QW light reflectance and absorption are determined by two closely situated discrete energy levels and by the difference of the refrection coefficient of the QW and barriers.
the quantum well is a very interesting object for the investigation of the interaction of light with matter.
the quantum well with two closely situated energy levels can be a source of the coherent light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QW light absorption and reflectance depend on the pulse shape.
the QW light reflectance is sensitive to the quantum well parameters and the pulse parameters.
the QW reflectance is a superposition of two components: the one corresponding to the QW exciton and the second one corresponding to a free carrier.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QW absorbance and reflectance may be strongly dependent on the pulse form and on the relationship of the radiatiive and nonradiative damping.
the light absorption and reflection spectra for a QW are very sensitive to the parameters of the QW and the stimulating pulse.
the QW reflectivity and absorbance may have pronounced resonances in a certain range of the stimulating pulse frequency.
